intro: Two print idioms use typography as visual material.
alt: A bright, tilted graphic layout beside a scuffed photocopy-like composition.

variants.name: New Wave typography
variants.look: Tilted axes and abrupt changes of scale disrupt the expected reading order.
variants.history: Wolfgang Weingart and designers influenced by him expanded Swiss typography through experiments in spacing, layering and offset printing.
variants.when: Break a rational grid to produce tension while keeping a focal point.
variants.why: Overlaps and contrasting scales create several possible routes through the visual field.

source.label: Macao Cultural Affairs Bureau · Weingart Typography

variants.name: grunge typography
variants.look: Ragged patches and distressed texture make the composition look reproduced and handled.
variants.history: In the 1990s, publications such as Ray Gun popularized distorted, layered and deliberately difficult typography.
variants.when: Give a layout the roughness and urgency of an ephemeral printed artifact.
variants.why: Distress patterns interrupt the visual uniformity associated with mechanical mass printing.

prompt: Draw a single textless art comparison board for a museum-quality online art atlas. Layout is two evenly split side-by-side cells, edge-to-edge, no gutters or borders; precise, strictly equally sized cells. Order is left to right within each row, then next row. Each cell is a distinct style treatment featuring the same female executive from reference, in original new art. The reference image is for identity only: recognizable ash-blonde hair in neat low bun with four-color windowpane hair clip, black-rimmed rectangular glasses over blue eyes, charcoal sheath dress under fitted black blazer, azure pocket square and blue lanyard with blank ID badge, holding a white coffee mug with a little four-color tile mark. Change the actual render style rather than adding only backgrounds. Layout styles in order: New Wave typography: electric pink and black asymmetrical deconstructed Swiss grid with generic illegible letter-shaped blocks at abrupt scales and diagonals crossing the photo portrait; grunge typography: xerox-distressed dry black stamp-shaped blocks, spills, ragged paper fragments, muddy olive and a grainy executive portrait. No readable words. No readable text, numbers, signatures, words, or extra panels.
